title: Using Experience Points
heading: Using Experience Points
summary: Explains how experience points raise Arts and Abilities and gives the cost formulas for gaining a level in each.
quotes: INCREASE AN ABILITY BY ONE: (Ability + 1) x 5 experience points
INCREASE AN ART BY ONE: Art + 1 experience points

title: Advancement Tables
heading: Advancement Tables
summary: Lookup table of the experience points needed to buy a score from zero, or to raise it by one, for Arts and Abilities.
quotes: To buy: The number of experience points required to raise a score from zero to that number.

title: Advancement Total
heading: Advancement
summary: Defines the Advancement Total earned by a season of study and the rule that only one source of experience may be used per season, apart from Exposure.
quotes: ADVANCEMENT TOTAL: Source Quality + Bonus from Virtues - Penalty from Flaws

title: Calculating Experience Points
heading: Calculating Experience Points
summary: Three-step procedure from Source Quality to Advancement Total to experience points gained, and which Virtues and Flaws modify each step.

title: Assigning Seasons
heading: Assigning Seasons
summary: Explains how seasons are abstractly assigned to work and study for ordinary characters, and how magi differ because lab work takes a whole real season and they have genuinely free seasons.

title: Gain Limit
heading: Limits
summary: A study source with its own level caps the score a student can reach from it, and gives no experience towards the next level.
quotes: This limit is called the Gain Limit.

title: Exposure
heading: Exposure
summary: The weakest source of experience: simply using or assisting with an Ability or Art during a season; experience may be split between two subjects, and lab work grants Exposure to lead magus and assistants.
quotes: EXPOSURE SOURCE QUALITY: Two

title: Adventure Experience
heading: Adventure
summary: Adventures give a whole season of experience with a Source Quality set by the storyguide, which can be split among Abilities used and Arts used on stage.
quotes: ADVENTURE SOURCE QUALITY: 5–10

title: Practice
heading: Practice
summary: Full-time self-directed study of an Ability, with special higher Source Qualities for native-tongue languages, Area Lore, feedback-rich crafts and practising spells for mastery; Arts cannot be raised this way.
quotes: PRACTICE SOURCE QUALITY: 4–8, usually 4

title: Training
heading: Training
summary: One-on-one instruction by a master who has a higher score and is using the Ability to earn a living; Hermetic Arts cannot be raised by training.
quotes: TRAINING SOURCE QUALITY: Master's score in Ability being taught + 3
TRAINING GAIN LIMIT: Master's score in Ability being taught

title: Worship
heading: Worship
requires: Christian character with access to a chapel or church (similar activities for other Divine faiths)
summary: A free-season devotional routine whose Source Quality is the Divine aura of the church, spent on Church Lore, Concentration, Music or Divine-aligned Abilities and Arts.
quotes: Worship has a Source Quality equal to the Divine aura in the church.

title: Teaching
heading: Teaching
summary: Lessons from a teacher with a higher score and a shared language, with Source Quality depending on the teacher's Communication and Teaching and a bonus that depends on class size; Arts may only be taught one-on-one.
quotes: TEACHING SOURCE QUALITY: Teacher's Communication + Teaching + 3 + bonus
TEACHING GAIN LIMIT: The teacher's score in the Art or Ability

title: Studying From Books
heading: Books
summary: Rules for studying summae and tractatus: language and literacy prerequisites, level limits for summae, one-time study of each tractatus, and Supernatural Abilities needing a score of at least one.
quotes: SUMMAE: Source Quality and Level
SUMMA GAIN LIMIT: Summa Level
TRACTATUS: Source Quality

title: Vis Study
heading: Vis
summary: Magi study an Art from raw vis, consuming pawns of that Art's vis for the season; a double botch on the stress die can lead to Wizard's Twilight.
quotes: VIS SOURCE QUALITY: Stress Die + Aura Bonus

title: Distractions
heading: Distractions
summary: Distractions of more than a month reduce an Advancement or writing total by a fraction for each full month lost, rounding fractions up.
quotes: For every full month lost, reduce the total by one third of its original amount.

title: Standard Texts (Roots and Branches of the Arts)
heading: Standard Texts
summary: Describes the widely available Roots of the Arts primers and the prized Branches of the Arts summae, which troupes may assign to Arts as needed for their saga.
quotes: These texts vary, but all have a Level of at least 7, and a Quality of at least 21.

title: Writing Books
heading: Writing Books
summary: Prerequisite scores for writing a useful book and the Source Quality formulas for summae and tractatus.
quotes: SUMMA SOURCE QUALITY: Author's Communication + 6 + bonus
Tractatus Source Quality: Author's Communication + 6

title: Writing Summae
heading: Summae
summary: How a summa's Level and Quality are chosen, the Quality bonus for a lower Level, and how many points per season accumulate until the book is finished, with a worked example.
quotes: the summa is complete.

title: Writing Tractatus
heading: Tractatus
summary: A tractatus takes one season to write and has a limit on how many one author can write in a given Art or Ability.
quotes: It takes one season to write a tractatus.

title: Copying Books
heading: Copying Books
summary: Careful copying keeps the original's quality; quick copying is three times as fast but lowers quality; the copyist's Profession: Scribe score drives the pace for summae.
quotes: COPYING CAREFULLY: 1 tractatus per season, or 6 + Profession (Scribe) points towards a summa.
COPYING QUICKLY: Three times as fast as careful copying, copy Source Quality is 1 lower than copied book.

title: Corrupted Copies
heading: Corrupted Copies
summary: Lists the minimum language, Realm Lore and Magic Theory scores a scribe needs to copy a text without corrupting it, since a corrupted text is useless.
quotes: A corrupted text is useless.

title: Hermetic Books: Definition of Categories of Value
heading: Hermetic Books: Definition of Categories of Value
summary: Sidebar giving typical Quality ranges for summae and tractatus (excellent, sound, vain, discarded and legendary books) as a function of Level.
quotes: These Summae have a Quality of (25 – Level) or below.

title: Acquiring Books
heading: Acquisition
summary: Overview of the Order's book trade: sale of finished books through Redcaps and Tribunals, and scribal hospitality in other covenants' libraries.
related: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.101

title: The Sale of Hermetic Books
heading: The Sale of Hermetic Books
summary: Describes the four postal sale methods (public offer, tender, exchange, subscription) and how books are sold at Tribunal.

title: Prices for Books and the Cow and Calf Oath
heading: Prices for Books
summary: Introduces the Cow and Calf Oath, a Hibernian ruling restricting resale or gifting of purchased copies, which the later price guidelines assume has been sworn.

title: Mundane Book Prices
heading: Mundane Books
summary: Mundane books are bought with cash from a stationer, with a delay of a season for uncommon titles and a cheaper unbound paper version available.

title: Hermetic Book Trade as Barter
heading: Books Concerning the Arts and Arcane Abilities
summary: Explains that Hermetic books are traded by barter and haggling, and that book values shift with events and with the vis a covenant holds.

title: Least Expensive Books
heading: Least Expensive Books
summary: Guidance on how damaged and discarded books are acquired, typically for about a pawn of vis per damaged summa, with cheap tractatus available in lots after a disaster.
quotes: A covenant wanting to purchase damaged summae with vis can usually find a seller for about a pawn of vis per book

title: Vain Book Prices
heading: Vain Books
summary: Pricing guidance for vain summae and tractatus, and the warning that a vanity book bought from someone other than its author costs as much as a sound one.
quotes: Characters can usually purchase vain summae for half their level in pawns of vis

title: Sound Book Prices
heading: Sound Books
summary: Guideline price in vis for ordering sound summae and tractatus from covenants with permanent copyists, including a surcharge for an immediately available copy.
quotes: These charge a number of pawns of vis equal to the book's level, if the purchaser is willing to wait a season for the copy to be produced.

title: Excellent Books
heading: Excellent Books
summary: Books of the highest Quality are normally gifts rather than purchases, with copying restricted; describes how Houses Bonisagus and Tremere handle them.

title: Learning Supernatural Abilities
heading: Learning Supernatural Abilities
requires: The Gift for Magic realm Abilities
summary: How a character first learns a Supernatural Ability by Training or Teaching, with a Source Quality penalty equal to scores in other Supernatural Abilities and a larger penalty if the Hermetic Arts have been opened.
quotes: SUPERNATURAL ABILITY SOURCE QUALITY: Normal Source Quality - Total Score in Supernatural Abilities

title: Training Creatures (Overview)
heading: Training Creatures
summary: Introduces taming of animals with a Cunning characteristic, by magi, magical characters or mundane handlers, followed by further training in tricks.

title: Taming Animals
heading: Taming Animals
summary: Taming is a seasonal activity accumulating points over consecutive seasons until they exceed the creature's Might; the tamer may split points among creatures of one species up to a limit set by Animal Handling.
quotes: REQUIRED POINTS TO TAME A CREATURE: Might of the Creature, Minimum 1

title: Taming Mundane Beasts
heading: Taming Mundane Beasts
summary: Sidebar giving mundane beasts an effective Might for taming purposes and noting that taming is a social activity so The Gift penalties apply.
quotes: mundane beasts have an effective (Animal) Might of 1 + 2 x Confidence Score

title: A Hermetic Tamer
heading: A Hermetic Tamer
summary: A magus tames an animal as a laboratory activity using a Rego (Form) Lab Total, producing a Lab Text that can later be reused to tame another creature of the same species.
quotes: TAMING POINTS ACCUMULATED EACH SEASON: Re(Fo) Lab Total – Creature's Might

title: Hermetic Bonuses to Taming Lab Total
heading: Hermetic Bonuses to Taming Lab Total
summary: List of bonuses added to a Hermetic taming Lab Total: Animal Handling, Animal Ken, Experimentation and similar Lab Texts.
quotes: Animal Handling Ability Score
Animal Ken Ability Score

title: A Magical Trainer
heading: A Magical Trainer
summary: Taming points per season for a character with the Master of (Form) Creatures Virtue, using Might, Animal Handling and Animal Ken minus the creature's Might.
quotes: Trainer's Might + Trainer's Animal Handling + Trainer's Animal Ken – Creature's Might

title: A Mundane Trainer
heading: A Mundane Trainer
summary: Taming points per season for a mundane handler, who can usually only tame beasts with a small Magic Might.
quotes: Int + Animal Handling + Animal Ken – Creature's Might

title: Tricks, Stunts, and Tasks
heading: Tricks, Stunts, and Tasks
summary: Who may command a tamed animal, and that a tamed animal is not considered to be under a continuing mystical effect.

title: Loyalty
heading: Loyalty
summary: A tamed creature gains a Loyal Personality Trait towards its tamer; Loyalty Tests and extra seasons of training can raise or transfer that loyalty.
quotes: LOYALTY TEST: Loyal Personality Trait + stress die vs Ease Factor

title: Training Animal Abilities
heading: Training Abilities
summary: A character with Animal Handling can train a tamed animal's existing Abilities with the standard training rules, and the troupe may allow new Abilities subject to a Loyalty test.
quotes: make a Loyalty test for the animal against an Ease Factor of 6

title: Trained Groups of Animals
heading: Trained Groups
summary: A handler may lead tamed animals in combat as a trained group, using Animal Handling in place of Leadership, with exceptions to the usual Combat Score matching.
quotes: The character's Animal Handling Ability score is used instead of his Leadership Ability score

title: Commanding a Creature
heading: Commanding a Creature
summary: Roll to command a tamed beast against an Ease Factor set by how unusual, frightening or dangerous the task is, with Loyalty tests required for the most extreme tasks.
quotes: COMMAND BEAST: Presence + Animal Handling (or Ride or Magic Lore) + stress die vs Ease Factor

title: Animal Ken and Animals
heading: Animal Ken
summary: A character with Animal Ken can reason with any animal using Animal Handling to get it to follow an instruction without taming it, and can give tamed animals more complex commands.

title: Changing Reputations
heading: Changing Reputations
summary: How noteworthy actions grant experience in a Reputation, how a bad Reputation can be supplanted by building a new one, and how multiple Reputations are rolled for.
quotes: Treat the Reputation as an Ability, and give the character one 'experience point' in it for every noteworthy action he performs.

title: Mystery Initiation
heading: Mystery Initiation
requires: Initiation into a Mystery cult (House Lore)
summary: Summary of how a Mystagogue's Initiation Total is compared with a Target Level (no die roll), including Target Levels, the effect of earlier Ordeals, and the minimum.
quotes: INITIATION TOTAL: Presence + (House) Lore + Script bonus
To Initiate a Minor Virtue known by the Mystagogue, the target level is 15
To Initiate a Major Virtue known by the Mystagogue, the target level is 21
related: The Mysteries Revised Edition, Chapter 2: Entering the Mysteries

title: The Initiation Script
heading: The Initiation Script
requires: Initiation into a Mystery cult (House Lore)
summary: A written text describing a successful Initiation, whose price may be an Ordeal, a Quest or a Sacrifice, and whose bonuses contribute to the Initiation Total if followed exactly.
related: The Mysteries Revised Edition, Chapter 2: Entering the Mysteries

title: Example Elements of an Initiation Script
heading: Example Elements of an Initiation Script
requires: Initiation into a Mystery cult (House Lore)
summary: Table of common Script bonuses for special place and time, Quests, sacrifices and Ordeals of varying severity.
quotes: Initiate has to complete a specific Quest

title: Varying a Script
heading: Varying a Script
requires: Initiation into a Mystery cult (House Lore)
summary: A Mystagogue may modify an Initiation Script with a test against an Ease Factor depending on whether a component is added or changed; only one change per Initiation is allowed.
quotes: Stress Die + Intelligence + (House) Lore vs. Ease Factor

title: Warping
heading: Warping
summary: Defines the Warping Score, advanced with Warping Points like an Ability, and gives the table of Warping Points needed per score.
quotes: To increase the Warping Score by one point, a character needs five times the new score extra Warping Points.

title: Warping and Non-Humans
heading: Warping and Non-Humans
summary: Mundane creatures and things can be warped, but the storyguide just describes effects; creatures with a Might score are immune to Warping.
quotes: Creatures with a Might score are absolutely immune to warping.

title: Gaining Warping Points
heading: Gaining Warping Points
summary: Lists the four separate sources of Warping Points, all of which stack.
quotes: Living in a strong (6 or higher) supernatural aura.

title: Warping from Living in Strong Auras
heading: Living in Strong Auras
summary: Table of Warping Points gained per period by aura strength and how much time is spent in the aura; characters whose own powers come from that realm are exempt.
quotes: Auras of over five points have an effect on anyone living within them

title: Warping from Powerful Supernatural Effects
heading: Powerful Supernatural Effects
summary: A Warping Point is gained from being subjected to a powerful supernatural effect not created by or specifically designed for you; sixth magnitude and higher Hermetic spells count.
quotes: any Hermetic spell of sixth magnitude or higher counts

title: Warping from Constant Supernatural Effects
heading: Constant Supernatural Effects
summary: Characters continuously under supernatural effects gain Warping Points over time regardless of effect strength; explains what counts as constant, exceptions such as Parma Magica, and a summary table of effect types.
quotes: A character who is constantly under the influence of one or more active supernatural effects gains one Warping Point per year for each effect.

title: Warping from Supernatural Botches
heading: Supernatural Botches
summary: Botching the roll to invoke a supernatural effect gives Warping Points equal to the number of zeros on the botch dice.
quotes: she gains one Warping Point for every zero on the botch dice.

title: Effects of Warping
heading: Effects of Warping
summary: What a rising Warping Score does to a character: more prone to Twilight for magi, and for mundane characters a progression of Minor Flaws, a supernatural Minor Virtue and then Major Flaws.
quotes: At a Warping Score of 6, and every point thereafter, the character gains a Major Flaw appropriate to the main sources of the warping.

title: Aging
heading: Aging
summary: Yearly aging roll against the Living Conditions and Longevity Ritual modifiers, the Aging table (apparent age, Aging Points, Decrepitude), and the Crisis procedure, table, medical attention and Creo Corpus remedies.
quotes: AGING TOTAL: Stress die (no botch) + age/10 (round up)
CRISIS TOTAL: Simple die + age/10 (round up) + Decrepitude Score
Characters begin aging in the Winter after they turn 35.

title: Combat Scores
heading: Combat Scores
summary: The five combat scores (Initiative, Attack, Defense, Damage, Soak) and the formulas for each total, plus Attack Advantage.
quotes: ATTACK TOTAL: Dexterity + Combat Ability + Weapon Attack Modifier + Stress Die
DEFENSE TOTAL: Quickness + Combat Ability + Weapon Defense Modifier + Stress Die
ATTACK ADVANTAGE: Attacker's Attack Total - Defender's Defense Total

title: Combat Botches
heading: Combat Botches
summary: Sidebar on how botched combat rolls reduce the total to zero (and why a botched Defense is so deadly), with an exception for combatants with a negative base Defense.
quotes: A botch on a combat roll reduces the total to zero, just as for any other botch.

title: Combat Sequence
heading: Combat Sequence
summary: Step-by-step combat round: one Initiative roll for the whole fight, parties act in decreasing order, attacker and defender each roll a stress die, and a hit deals damage minus Soak.
quotes: Initiative is determined once for the whole combat, and then remains the same every round.
If you miss, you cannot do any damage, no matter how high your Damage Total.

title: Length of a Combat Round
heading: Length of a Combat Round
summary: A combat round lasts about six seconds, which also determines how many rounds a Diameter spell lasts.
quotes: A combat round lasts for about six seconds, so that a Diameter Duration spell lasts for twenty rounds.

title: Spell Damage
heading: Spell Damage
summary: Sidebar explaining how a spell's listed damage is turned into a Damage Total with a stress die and how Soak is applied, and that Attack Advantage does not change spell damage.
quotes: The target's Soak Total + Stress Die is then subtracted from this to determine the wounds suffered.

title: Damage Table
heading: Damage Table
summary: Table converting damage past Soak into a wound level (Light to Dead) for each creature Size, with the rule for extrapolating beyond the table.
quotes: For every 5 + size points by which the Damage Total exceeds the Soak Total, the wound level increases by one.

title: Initiative Ties
heading: Initiative Ties
summary: Worked example of re-rolling tied Initiative, where the re-roll only orders the tied parties relative to each other.
quotes: The reroll only determines the relative ordering of C, D, and E; it does not over-ride the initial initiative result.

title: Combat: Simple Example
heading: Combat: Simple Example
summary: Worked example of two-party combat showing Initiative, Attack, Defense, botch checks, Attack Advantage, Soak, the Damage Table and Wound Penalties across two rounds.

title: Missile Combat
heading: Missile Combat
summary: Range increment penalties for missile attacks and the rule that only a shield's Defense bonus helps against missiles.
quotes: The Attack Total suffers a -3 penalty for every range increment beyond the first between the attackers and the defenders.

title: Moving in Combat
heading: Moving in Combat
summary: Three movement speeds in combat (walk, hurry, run) with pace-per-round formulas, and the length of a pace.
quotes: WALK: 10 + Qik – Encumbrance paces per round
HURRY: 2 x (10 + Qik – Encumbrance) paces per round
RUN: 4 x (10 + Qik – Encumbrance) paces per round

title: Groups
heading: Groups
summary: Basic rules for forming combat groups: size limit, roughly comparable Combat Totals, a vanguard, an optional leader, and when a group splits or reforms.
quotes: Groups are handled together for combat purposes, and may consist of one to six characters, inclusive.

title: Group Damage
heading: Group Damage
summary: A group deals its damage once per member, distributed as evenly as possible among the opposing group, with the vanguard taking at least as many blows and its wound penalties applying to the group.
quotes: The vanguard must always take at least as many blows as every other member of the group.

title: Untrained Group
heading: Untrained Group
summary: A group of similar-ability characters whose combat statistics are simply those of the vanguard.
quotes: Combat statistics are as for the vanguard.

title: Trained Group
heading: Trained Group
summary: Groups that have trained together get a leader, a limit on size from Leadership, and a bonus from the other members' combat abilities capped by the leader's Leadership, applied to either Attack or Defense.
quotes: The maximum number of fighters that can be coordinated is equal to the leader's Leadership score.

title: Defender
heading: Defender
summary: Characters (such as a magus with shield grogs) can be protected by defenders who fight as a group and the defended is only harmed if they fail.
quotes: The number of characters defended may not exceed the number of characters defending.

title: Defenders Without Groups
heading: Defenders Without Groups
summary: Sidebar allowing defenders even when the group rules are not used.
quotes: A defended character cannot be attacked until all his defenders have been incapacitated.

title: Disengaging
heading: Disengaging
summary: A party disengages by beating the Attack Totals of those who attacked it with a Defense Total, gaining a cumulative bonus on repeated attempts.
quotes: A party that tries to disengage repeatedly gets a +3 cumulative bonus for every attempt after the first

title: Exertion
heading: Exertion
summary: Spend a Fatigue level to add Combat Ability to an attack or to defense rolls for a round; groups must all spend a level and use the vanguard's Combat Ability.
quotes: By expending a Fatigue level you can add a bonus equal to your Combat Ability to either attack or defense for one round.

title: Magic in Combat
heading: Magic
summary: Magi cast at their Quickness-based place in the initiative order, take about a round to cast, and may fast-cast in response to other actions.
quotes: A magus Fast Casting a spell (see page 217) acts in immediate response to another action, and thus not at a particular initiative point.

title: Mounted Combat
heading: Mounted Combat
summary: A mounted fighter adds Ride, to a limit, to Attack and Defense Totals.
quotes: A mounted character adds his Ride score, to a maximum of +3, to his Attack and Defense Totals

title: Non-Lethal Combat (Scuffling and Grappling)
heading: Non-Lethal Combat
summary: Scuffles convert wound levels into lost Short-Term Fatigue, and grapples use Attack Advantage to build a Grapple Strength that the grappled character must reduce to escape.
quotes: A character attempting to grapple another succeeds if his Attack Advantage is greater than zero.
Fatigue levels inflicted in a scuffle are Short-Term Fatigue levels.

title: Scuffle Effects
heading: Scuffle Effects
summary: Table converting the wound level an attack would normally cause into Fatigue levels and lesser wounds in a scuffle.

title: Special Combat Effects (Maneuvers)
heading: Special Effects
summary: Non-damaging maneuvers such as tripping or disarming use the normal combat sequence with a target Attack Advantage required to succeed, usually based on Brawl.
quotes: Follow the normal combat sequence, and set an Attack Advantage needed to succeed.

title: Sample Advantages for Maneuvers
heading: Sample Advantages
summary: Table of required Attack Advantage for disarming, tripping, grabbing a worn item and taking a weapon.

title: Splitting Groups
heading: Splitting Groups
summary: Several attacking groups can try to break a defending group apart with an attack resolved on Attack Advantage rather than damage, dividing it evenly.
quotes: Groups may only try to split their opponents' groups in melee combat.

title: Combat: Complex Example
heading: Combat: Complex Example
summary: Worked example of group combat between a trained and an untrained group, showing the group bonus, re-rolled Initiative ties, Wound Penalties and disengaging.

title: Armor
heading: Armor
summary: Armor is described by its material and by how much of the body it covers, and its Protection adds to Soak.
quotes: Two factors describe the armor a given character wears: what it is made of and how much of it the character is wearing.

title: Armor Outfittings
heading: Outfittings
summary: Describes partial versus full armor and states that only the predominant material of a suit affects game statistics.
quotes: For simplicity, only the predominant material of the suit has any effect on game statistics (Protection and Load).

title: Armor Table
heading: Armor Table
summary: Table of Protection, Load and Cost for partial and full armor of each material.
quotes: The bonus the armor grants to the character's Soak score.

title: Melee Weapon Statistics
heading: Melee Weapon Statistics
summary: Table of Initiative, Attack, Defense and Damage modifiers, strength minimums, Load and Cost for brawling, single, and great melee weapons and shields.
quotes: The minimum strength requirements for a weapon and a shield must be met separately.

title: Missile Weapon Statistics
heading: Missile Weapon Statistics
summary: Table of thrown and bow weapons with modifiers, range increments, strength minimums, Load and Cost.
quotes: The range increment for the weapon, in paces.

title: Weapon Descriptions
heading: Weapon Descriptions
summary: Brief definitions of each weapon in the tables, including notes on how some are used (a lance only mounted, throwing weapons also usable in melee).
quotes: The lance may only be used from horseback, where it is a Single weapon.

title: Encumbrance
heading: Encumbrance
summary: Total Load from carried items determines Burden, and Strength offsets Burden to give Encumbrance, which is subtracted from many rolls though not from combat Attack and Defense when due to weapons and armor.
quotes: Burden increases when Load reaches the level for that Burden, so that a character with a Load of 9 has a Burden of 3.
If the character's Strength is zero or negative, his Encumbrance is the same as his Burden.

title: Fatigue Levels
heading: Fatigue
summary: Names the Fatigue levels from Fresh to Unconscious, explains that Short-Term and Long-Term losses share one track, and gives the penalties that apply to rolls other than Soak.
quotes: Most characters have six Fatigue levels
The penalty for Weary is -1, for Tired -3, and for Dazed -5.

title: Short-Term Fatigue
heading: Short-Term Fatigue
summary: Strenuous actions require a Fatigue roll on Stamina minus Encumbrance against an Ease Factor; failure costs a Short-Term Fatigue level and a botch costs two, with combat and magic using their own rules.
quotes: roll Stamina — Encumbrance on a stress die against an Ease Factor of 6

title: Recovery from Short-Term Fatigue
heading: Recovery from Short-Term Fatigue
summary: Fatigue is recovered one level at a time with rest, using the Fatigue Recovery Chart, with an optional Stamina roll to halve the time.
quotes: Success allows recovery in half the normal time.

title: Long-Term Fatigue
heading: Long-Term Fatigue
summary: Extended exertion costs Long-Term Fatigue levels at the storyguide's discretion, regained only by a good night's rest, with the more serious levels treated as short term.
quotes: One night's rest removes one Long-Term Fatigue level.

title: Fatigue Recovery Chart
heading: Fatigue Recovery Chart
summary: Table of the time needed to recover from each Fatigue level to the next lower one.

title: Wounds
heading: Wounds
summary: Damage beyond Soak becomes wounds; a character can have many wounds, their penalties add up and apply to all actions but not Soak, and non-fatal wounds cannot kill immediately.
quotes: The character suffers a penalty to all actions (rolls and totals) equal to the sum of all penalties due to his wounds

title: Damage Table (Wounds)
heading: Damage Table
summary: Repeat of the Damage Table converting damage past Soak into wound levels by Size.
quotes: For every 5 + size points by which the Damage Total exceeds the Soak Total, the wound level increases by one.

title: Wound Table
heading: Wound Table
summary: Table of the penalty each wound level applies to actions, with Incapacitated characters unable to act.
quotes: The character may not undertake any actions.

title: Activities While Injured
heading: Activities While Injured
summary: What a wounded character can safely do at each band of Wound Penalty, including travel, study and lab work, and the Recovery roll risked by overexertion.
quotes: Any character who does more than his injuries allow must make an immediate Recovery roll for his most serious wound.

title: Recovering From Wounds
heading: Recovering From Wounds
summary: Each wound gets a Recovery roll at an interval depending on its severity, compared with Stable and Improvement Ease Factors, so wounds may improve, hold steady with a bonus, or worsen.
quotes: RECOVERY TOTAL: Stamina + Medic's Chirurgy or Medicine score + Magical Aid + Stress Die
Recovery rolls do not suffer from the Wound Penalty.

title: Recovery from Incapacitation
heading: Recovery from Incapacitation
summary: Incapacitated characters make two Recovery rolls a day, dying on a low result and improving to Heavy on a high one, with a cumulative penalty otherwise.
quotes: On a roll of 0 or less, the character dies.

title: Medical Attention
heading: Medical Attention
summary: A medic's Chirurgy (for injuries) or Medicine (for disease and poison) adds to Recovery rolls; only one Ability can help with a given wound.
quotes: Combat wounds and similar injuries require Chirurgy, while diseases and poison require Medicine.

title: Healing Spells
heading: Healing Spells
summary: Creo Corpus rituals can heal wounds immediately, while other Creo Corpus spells add a bonus to Recovery rolls for as long as they remain in effect, and may cause Warping.
quotes: Certain Creo Corpus rituals can heal wounds immediately, without requiring a roll
related: ArM5 p.332 The Chirurgeon's Healing Touch

title: Debilitation
heading: Debilitation
summary: Diseases and poisons require a Stamina check against an Ease Factor set by the agent; failure means a wound treated with Medicine that then recovers by the usual rules.
quotes: Anyone exposed to a debilitating agent, whether poison or a cause of disease, must make a Stamina check against an Ease Factor set by the cause of the disease.

title: Diseases
heading: Diseases
summary: How diseases are modelled: humoral imbalances or disease spirits, handled via aging or debilitation, with Ease Factors indicating how much of a population is affected.
quotes: a disease with an Ease Factor of six will afflict about half of the population

title: Disease Table
heading: Disease Table
summary: Table of four sample diseases with the excess humor and symptoms of each.

title: Poisons
heading: Poisons
summary: Poison Ease Factors have a minimum and a maximum, and poisons can inflict fatal wounds from the start.
quotes: The Ease Factor for the initial Stamina check is at least 3

title: Poison Table
heading: Poison Table
summary: Table of sample poisons with their Ease Factor and the wound they cause.

title: Deprivation
heading: Deprivation
summary: Characters deprived of food, water or air make repeated Stamina checks with rising Ease Factor, losing Fatigue levels and then suffering worsening wounds.
quotes: The Ease Factor for the check starts at 3, and increases by one for every time period that passes.

title: Deprivation Table
heading: Deprivation Table
summary: Table of the time between checks for deprivation of air, water and food.

title: Injuries (Non-Combat Damage)
heading: Injuries
summary: Non-combat damage adds a damage bonus to a stress die and soak adds a stress die to Soak; the same rules calculate spell damage.
quotes: NON-COMBAT DAMAGE TOTAL: Damage Bonus + Stress Die
NON-COMBAT SOAK TOTAL: Soak Total + Stress Die.

title: Heat and Corrosion
heading: Heat and Corrosion
summary: Damage bonus from heat and corrosion is multiplied by how much of the body is exposed and inflicted once per combat round.
quotes: If it covers an entire limb, the damage bonus is doubled.

title: Heat and Corrosion Table
heading: Heat and Corrosion Table
summary: Table of intensity bonuses for common heat and corrosion sources.

title: Impact
heading: Impact
summary: Damage from falling or falling objects is taken once, with a table of sample impact damage bonuses.
quotes: Characters may also take damage from falling, or having things fall on them.

title: Travel
heading: Travel
summary: Guidelines for daily travel distances on foot, mounted, by cart and at sea, and the Long-Term Fatigue cost of hurried travel.
quotes: Attempts to travel quickly cost one Long-Term Fatigue level per day, as long as the characters actually travel.

title: Realms: Belonging and Affiliation
heading: Chapter 12: Realms
summary: Introduces the four realms and the difference between a creature belonging to a realm and merely being affiliated with it.
quotes: A creature that belongs to a realm cannot be affiliated with any other realm.

title: Realm Auras
heading: Realm Auras
summary: Auras rate how strongly a realm holds an area on a scale up to 10, usually act as a modifier on supernatural activity, and when two realms contest a place only the stronger holds sway at a time.
quotes: which can be rated in power on a scale from 1 to 10

title: Realm Interaction
heading: Realm Interaction
summary: An aura modifies all supernatural activity in it according to the Realm Interaction table and adds botch dice for acts in a foreign realm.
quotes: For each point of aura rating, roll an extra botch die.

title: Realm Interaction Table
heading: Realm Interaction Table
summary: Table of how each realm's aura modifies powers of each realm, with a worked example, and the rule that Divine powers are not hampered by other auras.
quotes: Divine powers have no penalty and no additional botch dice in auras of the other realms.

title: Supernatural Activity Rolls Modified by Aura
heading: Supernatural Activity Rolls Modified by Aura
summary: Sidebar listing which rolls and totals the aura modifier applies to: casting, lab totals, supernatural Ability rolls, Magic Resistance and Penetration.
quotes: Thus, a magus in a Magic aura of 4 has a +4 bonus to his Magic Resistance, while a demon has a -4 penalty.
The aura modifier does not apply to Penetration twice.

title: Creatures of a Realm
heading: Creatures of a Realm
summary: Guidance on how a creature's realm shapes its attitude towards humans (Infernal, Magic, Divine, Faerie), illustrated with a talking dog in each realm.
quotes: Creatures of the Infernal are always interested in corrupting and harming human beings

title: Magic Resistance and Penetration of Creatures
heading: Magic Resistance and Penetration
summary: Creatures with a Might Score derive Magic Resistance and Penetration from it, and characters with non-Hermetic supernatural abilities have their own Penetration formula.
quotes: CREATURE MAGIC RESISTANCE: Might Score + Aura Modifier
CREATURE PENETRATION: Might Score – (5 x Might Points spent on power) + Penetration Bonus + Aura Modifier
CHARACTER PENETRATION: Effect Roll – Ease Factor + Penetration Bonus + Aura Modifier

title: Magical Auras
heading: Magical Auras
summary: Describes typical strengths and character of Magic auras, where covenants are usually sited, and the dangers of the strongest auras; Magic auras do not vary cyclically.
quotes: Most magical areas have an aura from 1 to 5.

title: Sources of Magical Auras
heading: Sources of Magical Auras
summary: How Magic auras arise from fine natural features or from magical creatures and activity, and the usual upper limits on the strengths produced.
quotes: If a moderately powerful (Might 30 or more) magical creature takes up residence in an area, that place will, over the course of years, acquire a weak Magical aura.

title: Infernal Creatures
heading: Infernal Creatures
summary: Infernal creatures may take attractive forms, and their lies cannot be detected by Magic realm powers, though ordinary investigation can still reveal the truth.
quotes: The lies of creatures that belong to the Infernal realm cannot be detected by the powers of the Magic realm.

title: Infernal Auras
heading: Infernal Auras
summary: Describes the effects of Infernal auras on travelers and magic, that magic can detect them, and that they wax at night and wane on holy days.
quotes: Of greater concern to magi, Infernal auras interfere with the use of magic.
related: Realms of Power: The Infernal, pp.10-17

title: Sources of Infernal Auras
heading: Sources of Infernal Auras
summary: Infernal auras arise from serious or repeated sin and from infernal creatures or powers, with examples of the strengths produced.
quotes: In an area with no aura, a cruel and premeditated murder can create a level 1 aura.

title: Faerie Creatures
heading: Faerie Creatures
summary: Faeries gain Vitality when humans play out their stories, cannot truly create, change or learn without mortal aid, and are predictable if you know their story.
quotes: They are interested in having humans play out their stories, because faeries gain energy, called Vitality, when this happens.

title: Faerie Auras
heading: Faerie Auras
summary: Faerie auras range from weak to immense and vary in strength with how closely the surroundings match the nature of the faeries within.
quotes: Faerie auras tend to vary in strength depending on how closely the surrounding world matches the nature of the faeries within.

title: Sources of Faerie Auras
heading: Sources of Faerie Auras
summary: Faerie auras arise from faeries, their powers, and stories told about a place, and tend to be stronger than other aura types.
quotes: Faerie auras also arise when stories are told about a place.

title: Divine Auras
heading: Divine Auras
summary: Divine auras (the Dominion) are nearly ubiquitous where believers live, strengthen on Sundays and holy days, and wane at night and on evil days.
quotes: On Sundays and holy days the power of the Dominion increases; at night and on evil days it wanes.

title: Sources of Divine Auras
heading: Sources of Divine Auras
summary: Typical Divine aura strengths for fields, villages, towns, places of worship, relic sites and the holiest places.
quotes: Most places of worship have an aura of 4, while places with wider significance, such as cathedrals, important mosques, and the churches of major monasteries, have an aura of 5.
related: Realms of Power: The Divine Revised Edition, pp.10-17

title: True Faith
heading: True Faith
summary: True Faith is measured by a Score and Faith Points that work like Confidence, and the Score gives Magic Resistance; Faith Points are regained each dawn up to the Score.
quotes: TRUE FAITH MAGIC RESISTANCE: True Faith Score X 10
Each dawn, you regain a number of Faith Points up to your True Faith Score
related: Realms of Power: The Divine Revised Edition, p.56

title: Relics
heading: Relics
summary: Every relic has Faith giving Confidence-like Faith Points and Magic Resistance, a Divine Might limiting uses of its powers, and a power that repels Infernal creatures.
quotes: A relic's Divine Might is equal to the relic's Faith score (or highest Faith score, if more than one applies) multiplied by 10, and the Might Pool is refreshed with every sunrise.
related: Realms of Power: The Divine Revised Edition, pp.88-89

title: Miracles
heading: Miracles
summary: Miracles are direct divine intervention and cannot fail or be resisted.
quotes: As such, they can do anything, cannot fail, and cannot be resisted by any other power.

title: Magic Resistance For Church Officers and Sovereigns
heading: Magic Resistance For Church Officers and Sovereigns
summary: Sidebar giving ordained and anointed leaders Magic Resistance by rank, a Soak bonus derived from it, and the effect of excommunication.
quotes: The religious and secular leaders listed below receive a Magic Resistance score as listed here, and a Soak bonus equal to Magic Resistance / 5.

title: The Mundane
heading: The Mundane
summary: Mundane areas have no aura, so powers work there without hindrance, though most settlements share somewhat in the Dominion.
quotes: The mundane has no aura rating

title: Regiones
heading: Regiones
summary: Introduces regiones, layered levels of aura at one physical location whose higher levels have stronger auras and stranger inhabitants.
quotes: Regiones consist of several levels of aura, layered one on top of another in order of increasing power, the lowest level is connected to the mundane world.

title: Entering and Leaving Regiones
heading: Entering and Leaving Regiones
summary: The three ways into a regio (being led, entering voluntarily by sight or path, or getting lost) and the roll and Ease Factor for seeing into a regio level.
quotes: REGIO SIGHT ROLL: Perception + Appropriate Ability + Stress Die
EASE FACTOR: 5 + (2 × difference between current level's aura and sought level's aura)

title: Magic in Regiones
heading: Magic in Regiones
summary: Powers used in a regio level are modified by that level's aura per the Realm Interaction Table, with doubled botch dice for powers of a different realm.
quotes: any power used within a regio of a realm different from that of the power attracts twice the normal number of botch dice.

title: The Origins of Regiones
heading: The Origins of Regiones
summary: Two common ways regiones arise (a besieged aura moving up, or a powerful event creating a new level), and that Hermetic magi cannot create them at will.

title: Vis Sources
heading: Vis Sources
summary: Explains what a vis source is, the Art and amount of vis it normally yields, and how vis must be gathered.
quotes: Sometimes, however, it is possible to take a certain number of pawns of vis from a place every year.

title: Tainted Vis
heading: Tainted Vis
summary: Vis from Faerie, Divine and Infernal auras may be tainted, with Infernal vis adding botch dice to spellcasting and demanding an experimental-results roll for enchanted items.
quotes: At the very least, using Infernally tainted vis adds twice as many botch dice as usual to spellcasting
related: Realms of Power: The Infernal, pp.18-19

title: Creature Might
heading: Creature Might
summary: Might Score gives a supernatural creature Magic Resistance, fuels its powers through the Might Pool and sets Penetration; the Pool normally refreshes over a day.
quotes: A creature that hasn't used any powers recently has a Might Pool equal to its Might Score.
Might Pools almost always refresh to the creature's Might Score over the course of a day.
CREATURE MAGIC RESISTANCE: Might Score + Aura Modifier

title: Creature Powers
heading: Creature Powers
summary: Creature powers have no levels and instead cost Might points, with a standard format, a Penetration formula based on Might and cost, and a dispelling level equal to Might.
quotes: Power Name, X points, Init Y, Form: Description.
CREATURE POWER PENETRATION: Might Score – (5 x Might Point cost of the power) + Penetration Bonus
CREATURE POWER LEVEL FOR DISPELLING: Creature's Might Score

title: Creature Format
heading: Creature Format
summary: Line-by-line explanation of a creature's stat block (Might, Characteristics with Cunning, Size, Confidence, Fatigue and Wound Penalty notation, Abilities, Powers, Vis).
quotes: Size 0 is the same size (volume, and thus normally roughly mass) as an adult human being.
An increase or decrease of three points of Size is approximately equivalent to a factor of ten change in size.

title: Size Examples
heading: Size Examples
summary: Table of Size values with approximate heights, weights and example creatures, and the rule of thumb that each Size category roughly doubles weight.
quotes: Each Size category is approximately twice as heavy as the previous size category.

title: Creating Creatures
heading: Creating Creatures
summary: Advice for storyguides designing creatures: start from a concept and role, then choose Might, combat statistics and power costs to suit the intended challenge.
quotes: A Might Score of 20 indicates that starting magi will have a lot of trouble affecting the creature with magic.

title: Beasts in Combat
heading: Beasts in Combat
summary: Beasts can use most human combat options, usually fight as untrained groups, and may use only one natural weapon per round, the best listed first.
quotes: Regardless of how many weapons a beast has, it may only attack with one weapon in a given round.

title: Creating Mundane Beasts
heading: Creating Mundane Beasts
summary: Introduces the step-by-step method for building statistics for any mundane beast, for example a shapechanger's animal form.

title: Beast Creation Step 1: Type and Size
heading: 1. Type and Size
summary: Beasts are sorted into four categories (Birds, Fish, Hoofed Beasts and Clawed Beasts), which drive later steps.
quotes: There are four categories of beasts: Birds, Fish, Hoofed Beasts and Clawed Beasts.

title: Beast Creation Step 2: Characteristics
heading: 2. Characteristics
summary: Beasts use Cunning instead of Intelligence, spend characteristic points only on the four physical Characteristics, then adjust Strength and Quickness for Size; mental Characteristics come from the beast's type.
quotes: Unlike human characters, animals only spend points on their four physical characteristics (Stamina, Strength, Dexterity and Quickness).
Add twice the Size to Strength
Subtract Size from Quickness

title: Mental Characteristics of Creatures
heading: Mental Characteristics of Creatures
summary: Table of Cunning, Perception, Presence and Communication for each beast type.

title: Example Physical Characteristics of Creatures
heading: Example Physical Characteristics of Creatures
summary: Table of typical Size and physical Characteristics for common kinds of animal, as starting points for new beasts.

title: Creatures of Non-Standard Size
heading: Creatures of Non-Standard Size
summary: How to scale a creature larger or smaller than average, such as after a Muto Animal spell, by adjusting Strength, Quickness and wound ranges per Size point.
quotes: for every point of Size removed, subtract two from Strength (and therefore Damage total), add one to Quickness (and therefore Initiative and Defense totals), and decrease the damage range for each wound level by 1 (minimum of 1)

title: Beast Creation Step 3: Virtues and Flaws
heading: 3. Virtues and Flaws
summary: Species Virtues and Flaws come free to all members of a species and are not balanced for game purposes, while exceptional individuals need balanced individual Virtues and Flaws.
quotes: It is recommended that a species have at least one point of Flaws for every three points of Virtues.

title: Suitable Virtues and Flaws for Beasts
heading: Suitable Virtues and Flaws
summary: Lists Virtues and Flaws appropriate to beasts and a note that Improved Characteristics grants more characteristic points to larger creatures.
quotes: A creature of Size +1 or smaller gets 3 characteristic points from this Virtue as normal, a creature of Size +2 gets 6 characteristic points, a creature of size +3 gets 9 characteristic points, and so on.

title: Beast Creation Step 4: Basic Abilities
heading: 4. Basic Abilities
summary: Table of the Abilities every creature of each type has, plus rules that animals with Cunning cannot gain experience or learn new Abilities as adults except through an Animal Handling teacher.
quotes: Animals (at least, those with Cunning rather than Intelligence) cannot acquire experience points to improve their Abilities once they have reached adulthood, nor can they learn new Abilities.

title: Beast Creation Step 5: Qualities
heading: 5. Qualities
summary: Catalog of creature Qualities (such as Ambush Predator, Constriction, Grapple, Overrun, Swallow Whole, Tough Hide and Venomous) that adjust characteristics, Abilities, Protection and special attacks, with how extra Fatigue levels are granted.
quotes: One extra Fatigue level grants an additional Winded level, two extra grant another Winded Level and another Weary Level, etc.

title: Beast Creation Step 6: Combat Statistics
heading: 6. Combat Statistics
summary: A beast's combat totals are calculated as normal using the Natural Weapons Table.
quotes: Combat Statistics are calculated as normal (page 393), using the Natural Weapons Table.

title: Natural Weapons Table
heading: Natural Weapons Table
summary: Table of Initiative, Attack, Defense and Damage modifiers for natural weapons such as teeth, claws, horns and hooves.
quotes: All natural weapons use the Brawl Ability.

title: Aging of Animals
heading: Aging
summary: Adjusts the age at which aging starts, the age modifier and the number of aging rolls per year for an animal from its average lifespan relative to a human's.
quotes: Thus a creature with an average lifespan of 10 years has a modifier of (50/10) or five.

title: Statistics of Shapechangers
heading: Statistics of Shapechangers
requires: Shapechanger (for example House Bjornaer Heartbeast or Skinchanger)
summary: Introduces the seven-step procedure for combining a human's and an animal species' statistics into those of a shapechanger's animal form.

title: Shapechanger Step 1: Characteristics
heading: 1. Characteristics
requires: Shapechanger (for example House Bjornaer Heartbeast or Skinchanger)
summary: For each Characteristic other than Intelligence/Cunning, take the lower value if both are negative, the higher if both are positive, and otherwise add the two.
quotes: If the human and the animal Characteristic are both negative, use the lower of the two.
If the human and the animal Characteristic are both positive, use the higher of the two.

title: Shapechanger Step 2: Cunning Versus Intelligence
heading: 2. Cunning Vs. Intelligence
requires: Shapechanger (for example House Bjornaer Heartbeast or Skinchanger)
summary: Shapechangers normally keep human Intelligence, though lycanthropes lose it for Cunning; a worked example combines a magus's and a wolf's Characteristics.
quotes: In most cases, the shapechanger retains human Intelligence.

title: Shapechanger Step 3: Size
heading: 3. Size
requires: Shapechanger (for example House Bjornaer Heartbeast or Skinchanger)
summary: The animal form uses the animal's Size; a Size-affecting Virtue or Flaw makes the character a notably large or small member of the species.
quotes: Human Size has no impact on the Size statistic of the shapechanged form.

title: Shapechanger Step 4: Virtues and Flaws
heading: 4. Virtues & Flaws
requires: Shapechanger (for example House Bjornaer Heartbeast or Skinchanger)
summary: Virtues and Flaws of both human and animal forms apply in animal form, but a duplicate applies only once.
quotes: If the animal form already has a Virtue or Flaw possessed by the character, it applies only once.

title: Shapechanger Step 5: General Abilities
heading: 5. General Abilities
requires: Shapechanger (for example House Bjornaer Heartbeast or Skinchanger)
summary: A shapechanged character uses the animal form's General Abilities, keeping only languages, lores, Supernatural Abilities and (if Intelligence is retained) Arcane and Academic Abilities.
quotes: Use the General Abilities of the animal form.

title: Shapechanger Step 6: Communicating
heading: 6. Communicating
requires: Shapechanger (for example House Bjornaer Heartbeast or Skinchanger)
summary: A shapechanger can communicate with animals of the same or similar species, grouped by temperament, aspect, diet and habitat.
quotes: Acquire the ability to communicate with members of the same or similar species as the shapechanged form.

title: Shapechanger Step 7: Wounds and Experience
heading: 7. Wounds & Experience
requires: Shapechanger (for example House Bjornaer Heartbeast or Skinchanger)
summary: Wounds carry between human and animal forms (lycanthropes heal animal-form wounds on reverting), and experience gained in animal form may go to animal-form Abilities.
quotes: Any wounds taken in the human form are reflected in the animal form, and vice versa.
